headline_marked: [[Huawei enters South Korea's AI chip market]] with Atlas SuperPods, claims 3x H20 inference at 1/4 cost
headline: Huawei enters South Korea's AI chip market with Atlas SuperPods, claims 3x H20 inference at 1/4 cost
summary: Huawei plans to launch its Ascend 950 series processors and Atlas 950 SuperPod platform in Q4 2026. It reportedly offers 2.87x Nvidia H20 inference performance at one-quarter the cost, aiming to challenge Nvidia's market dominance.
details: Huawei is reportedly planning to enter South Korea's AI accelerator market in Q4 2026. It will introduce its Ascend 950 series processors and Atlas 950 SuperPod AI computing platform, aiming to challenge Nvidia's dominance with claims of significantly higher performance at a fraction of the cost.

The rollout includes the inference-focused Ascend 950PR, which began mass production in April, and the training-oriented Ascend 950DT, set for Q4 release. These chips will debut alongside the Atlas 950 SuperPod, an integrated platform scalable to 8,192 Ascend processors.

Huawei Korea has already secured master distributor agreements with local partners Hansol PNS and SK Shieldus. Preparations for commercialization are underway, focusing on aggressive pricing and powerful processing capabilities to attract customers.

The Ascend 950PR reportedly delivers 2.87 times the inference performance of Nvidia's H20 AI accelerator at roughly one-quarter the cost. Huawei admits its chip doesn't match Nvidia's H200, but suggests clustering thousands of Ascend processors can bridge the performance gap.

Huawei's strategy targets South Korea's surging AI infrastructure demand, positioning its hardware as a cost-effective alternative to Nvidia. The company is also working to improve compatibility between its CANN software stack and Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem to ease developer migration.

Despite previous market entry success in LTE, Huawei is expected to face resistance due to local sensitivity to Chinese technology and security concerns. Other challenges include the power/heat overhead of high-density silicon and the risk of vendor lock-in with a proprietary stack.

headline_marked: [[Bentley teases Torcal]], its first EV, fully revealing it September 23rd
headline: Bentley teases Torcal, its first EV, fully revealing it September 23rd
summary: Bentley's first all-electric vehicle, the Torcal, will be officially unveiled in London on September 23rd. The luxury automaker promises it will set "extraordinary benchmarks."
details: Bentley has confirmed its first all-electric vehicle, the Torcal, will be fully revealed in London on September 23rd. CEO Frank-Steffern Walliser stated it "sets extraordinary benchmarks in every area that matters."

The Torcal will join Bentley's existing lineup, taking its name from Spain's El Torcal de Antequera rock formation and the Latin word for "torque." Bentley first announced plans for an electric SUV in 2021.

The vehicle was previously spotted testing in the Arctic Circle and at Germany's Nurburgring, showing a fastback-like aesthetic. Spy photos revealed an interior with red leather, black Alcantara, and a large curved display.

Bentley has promised more updates on the Torcal in the weeks leading up to the September 23rd reveal. The company emphasizes that the new EV will carry forward the brand's defining craftsmanship and performance.
